what_happened:
The furthest this campaign has reached since attempt5. Every pre-provider gate passed, the pod's own test suite passed, the continuation delivered 8.06 MiB of evidence while leaving 22.213 GiB of checkpoints where they were, and the driver detached under its own descriptor probe.

Stages P, S and R then PASSED. Stage P built BOTH arms and announced them durable -- the candidate 1a2b5b030e7e4e202fda3a810ed53c5f and incumbent_b -- over about fifty-one minutes. Stage S and Stage R passed because every screening probe of this campaign is already trained and validly scored, so there was nothing to run and a committed ranking to read.

Stage C raised in `require_probe_headroom`, BEFORE training the first probe it owed. Nothing was trained and nothing was scored: probes_trained 0, probes_scored 0. No formal measurement began, so there is no measurement to retry and no science to pool.
root_cause:
`probe_local_need_bytes` derives the storage bound from the model's parameter count, reading `self.required_identity` when an arm has been built this session and falling back to `BH.candidate_manifest(REPO)[0]['num_parameters']` otherwise. `candidate_manifest` joins the frozen selection to the durable products on the machine that froze them, so it needs bytes a pod never receives -- and it raised for candidate d005dfb27e7bb5adc46eb988ae79e2a9 at /root/aad-artifacts/phase_c2_full_search/attempt3_replay.

The fallback is reached by every CONTINUATION and only by a continuation. `required_identity` is set when an arm is built for a rung; a continuation's screening probes are all already scored, so no arm is built for one; stage C is then the first rung to ask. attempt5 never took this branch because it trained screening probes immediately after building arms. So the line's first execution was on a paid pod, in stage C, fifty-one minutes in.

It asked a question the selection already answers: `num_parameters` is committed for every candidate, the selection is committed evidence, and it ships in the bundle.
repair: `BH.candidate_parameter_count` reads the count from the frozen selection alone -- no join, no host bytes -- and refuses if the five candidates disagree, since they are meant to share an architecture. The driver's fallback uses it.
a_skip_that_hid_a_defect: The tests covering this exact branch were the ones I had marked `needs_host_local_stores` two attempts earlier. They failed with the store hidden, I read that as 'these cases need host bytes', and marked them -- when the truth was 'the code under test wrongly needs host bytes'. That silenced the tests that would have caught this for $0. The declared skip set has gone from 28 to 8: twenty of those cases now run under a pod-like filesystem, and what remains genuinely needs the products' BYTE SIZES via `storage_requirement`, which no pod path reaches.
regression: 239 passed on the dev box; 231 passed and 8 skipped under a pod-like filesystem, where before the repair the same set gave 7 failures. Both mutations -- driver reverts to `candidate_manifest`; the count function joins the store anyway -- fail the two new tests under pod-like conditions.
the_arms_were_not_preserved_and_that_is_: Both arms were built and announced durable and were not fetched off-pod. They are digest-pinned fixed paths, so a rebuild reproduces them byte for byte; at 1.19 GB each, restoring 2.4 GB to a replacement pod over this host's 0.72 MB/s uplink is about 55 minutes against about 51 to rebuild. Moving them would cost more than making them, so the working set stays empty -- which is the same rule as P8.4, applied to an artifact that is cheaper to recompute than to transport.
why_a_fresh_chain: the repair touches the driver and behavioural.py, both in the executable closure, so the closure moved and attempt11's authorization and bundle no longer bind this tree.
consumed: $1.2180 all-in for 66.03 minutes of L40S. One provider resource, created and provider-confirmed deleted behind its teardown gate. No training, no scoring, no measurement.
